newsitem.title: USA: Police move in striking distance of Texas rebels.
newsitem.headline: Police move in striking distance of Texas rebels.

text.p: Elite police units moved within striking distance late on Friday of armed Texas separatists holed up in a mountain compound and officials said the rebels were preparing for a shootout.
Texas Department of Public Safety spokesman Mike Cox said members of the self-styled Republic of Texas had been ordered to open fire on the advancing police units although no shots had been fired.
Cox said one Republic member was heard over radio frequency ordering others to "fire at will" and "put the laser on him (a police officer) and pluck him."

He described the advance of Special Weapons and Tactics Teams (SWAT) as a "major tactical operation where substantial ground was covered" and that the units were within 440 yards of the compound where Republic leader Richard McLaren and six followers were hiding.

Police, who had been deployed two miles away, were ordered to advance after minimal progress in negotiations aimed at coaxing McLaren and the other separatists, who believe Texas is an independent nation, to surrender.
Cox refused to say if or when police planned to raid the compound, but said they had "bent over backwards" to accommodate McLaren's demands with little to show for it.
